lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Wait. Same case?

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: Same case. Same data. Two independently trained models — 25.09 versus 96.95.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: So which one drives the decision?

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: Neither, by itself. The disagreement becomes a governed signal.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: So what happens underneath that decision?

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: The model is only one part of it. Signal Intelligence. Risk Intelligence. Decision Governance.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: Together, they form RiskModelForgeIQ's Decision Intelligence Layer.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: So this is more than MLOps?

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: Exactly. MLOps manages the model. DecisionOps governs what happens when the model actually makes a decision — the rules, the versions, human review, explainability, the evidence behind it.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Why are they so different?

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: The champion sees this case as relatively routine. The challenger sees something materially different.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: RiskModelForgeIQ doesn't hide that disagreement behind a blended score. It makes the disagreement operational.
__VISUAL_71.86_POINT_DISAGREEMENT__
__VISUAL_HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED__

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: So the system doesn't pick a winner?

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: Right. When the models disagree this sharply, a human does.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: We don't stop at explaining the score. We can trace the decision back through the model, the contributing signal, and the underlying evidence.
__VISUAL_DECISION_SCORE_RULE_FEATURE_SOURCE__

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: Real Medicare Part B claims, peer-grouped by specialty and region — not a synthetic example built to make a point.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: What about the rules underneath the models — are those just hardcoded somewhere?

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: The rule changes. The system creates a new version. The previous version is frozen.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: If the change doesn't perform, rollback is one switch.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: Every historical decision still points to the version that made it.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Did that actually matter?

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: This is the surprising part.
__VISUAL_2.8_TO_15.2_ESCALATION__

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: Measured precision moved from 2.8 percent to 15.2 percent.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: The model didn't change.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: The decision rules did.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Six months from now, if someone asks which model made this decision — can you prove it?

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: The registry answers that. Model. Version. Role. Status.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: And can we reproduce the original decision?

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: Yes. It stays tied to the exact model, rule, and policy version that produced it.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Does that same traceability hold model-wide, not just case by case?

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: It does. Ranked by real contribution — not a black-box weight.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: The platform also watches the assumptions underneath the model.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: When the distribution of an important feature changes, the system can surface that — before performance quietly degrades.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: On this demo, that's seeded traffic, not live trade data — but it's the same mechanism that would run in production.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: These aren't separate features.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: They're one governed decision lifecycle.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: That's the difference between deploying a model and governing a decision.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: So the model is only part of the architecture.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: Exactly.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: MLOps manages the model.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: DecisionOps governs the decision. That's RiskModelForgeIQ.

lines.speaker: Rahul
lines.text: The demo link is in the comments.
